title: Shelf grid: stagger entrance animation
description:
## Parent

shelf-proving-ground-djk (Shelf grid spec)

## What to build

Cards animate into the grid with a staggered entrance: each card fades in (opacity 0 to 1) and translates up (translateY 8px to 0). Per-card stagger delay is 50ms. Duration is --shelf-motion-duration-fast. Easing is --shelf-motion-easing-enter.

The stagger fires on initial page load (after skeletons swap to real cards) and again on every filter change. On filter change, all visible cards re-stagger (re-key the filtered list so React remounts).

Stagger is capped at 20 cards. Cards beyond index 20 appear at full opacity instantly — no animation, no delay. This prevents a 10-second waterfall on the many fixture (200 books).

Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, all cards appear simultaneously with no translate and no stagger. The motion tokens collapse to 0ms, so cards are visible immediately. Ensure no card is stuck at opacity 0.

The entrance animation must stay within the frame budget: at most 2 long frames (>50ms gap) during the stagger sequence.

## Acceptance criteria

[ ] Shelf grid: cards stagger in on load with correct tokens (@motion)
[ ] Shelf grid: cards re-stagger on filter change (@motion)
[ ] Shelf grid: stagger capped at 20 cards (@motion)
[ ] Shelf grid: reduced motion shows no translate and no stagger (@motion)
[ ] Shelf grid: entrance animation within frame budget (@perf)

## Tests to turn green

File: e2e/acceptance/shelf-grid.spec.ts
Run: npx playwright test --grep "@djk\.3" --grep-invert "@visual"
Run visual: npm run ui:qa -- --grep "@djk\.3.*@visual"

## Blocked by

Ticket 1: Shelf grid: page load with grid and skeletons
Ticket 2: Shelf grid: filter chips (re-stagger test needs working filters)

title: Shelf grid: filter chips
description:
## Parent

shelf-proving-ground-djk (Shelf grid spec)

## What to build

The filter chip bar becomes interactive. Tapping a status chip narrows the grid to books with that status. Multi-select is supported: tap "To Read" then "Reading" to see both. "All" means no active filter — it is selected when no status chips are pressed. Tapping "All" resets. Deselecting all status chips returns to "All."

Chips toggle via click, Enter, and Space. Each chip is a button with aria-pressed reflecting its state.

The aria-live="polite" region (already in the DOM from ticket 1) announces the filtered count after every change (e.g. "Showing 2 books", "Showing all 6 books").

When the filtered list is empty (books exist but none match), the grid area shows centered muted text: "No books match this filter." No CTA, no illustration. (Note: no current seed fixture produces this state — all three statuses have books. The builder should add a targeted test in e2e/agent/ to verify this path.)

## Acceptance criteria

[ ] Shelf grid: filtering by one status shows matching books
[ ] Shelf grid: filtering by multiple statuses
[ ] Shelf grid: deselecting all chips returns to "All"
[ ] Shelf grid: tapping "All" resets filter
[ ] Shelf grid: keyboard can toggle filter chips

## Tests to turn green

File: e2e/acceptance/shelf-grid.spec.ts
Run: npx playwright test --grep "@djk\.2" --grep-invert "@visual"
Run visual: npm run ui:qa -- --grep "@djk\.2.*@visual"

title: Shelf grid: page load with grid and skeletons
description:
## Parent

shelf-proving-ground-djk (Shelf grid spec)

## What to build

Navigate to the shelf and see the complete page-load flow: 6 skeleton cards appear instantly while the API responds, then hard-swap to a responsive grid of placeholder cards showing all books newest-first.

The page renders inside a <main> wrapper. The grid is a <ul role="list"> with <li> per card. Placeholder cards show title text, author text, and a badge-shaped element (the Book card ticket owns the full card design later).

Skeleton cards have two shimmer bars (title-height + author-height) and a small pill placeholder (top-right). Shimmer is an opacity pulse using the slow motion token. Under reduced motion, skeletons are static. Transition to real cards is a hard swap (skeletons unmount, cards appear).

The grid uses CSS auto-fill/minmax(280px, 1fr), capped at 4 columns via ~1280px max-width centered. Gap is space-lg. Page padding is space-md on mobile, space-lg at 768px+. Cards stretch to the tallest in their row (grid default).

A filter chip bar renders above the grid with "All" selected by default (the chip bar is structural here — filtering behavior comes in the next ticket). The bar is a div with role="group" and aria-label="Filter by status". Chips are buttons with aria-pressed. Order: All | To Read | Reading | Finished. Chip gap is space-sm. Selected chip has accent fill; unselected has subtle border; radius-full pills.

An aria-live="polite" region exists in the DOM (the next ticket populates it with announcements).

No stagger animation in this ticket — cards appear at full opacity.

## Acceptance criteria

[ ] Shelf grid: shows all books by default
[ ] Shelf grid: newest-first order
[ ] Shelf grid: "All" chip is selected on load
[ ] Shelf grid: shows skeleton cards while loading
[ ] Shelf grid: chip visual states (@visual)
[ ] Shelf grid: default populated screenshot (@visual)
[ ] Shelf grid: skeleton loading screenshot (@visual)
[ ] Shelf grid: no horizontal overflow at any width (@layout)
[ ] Shelf grid: 1 column on mobile (@layout)
[ ] Shelf grid: 2 columns on tablet (@layout)
[ ] Shelf grid: 3-4 columns on desktop, max 4 (@layout)
[ ] Shelf grid: skeleton shimmer respects motion preference (@motion)
[ ] Shelf grid: no layout shift when skeleton swaps to cards (@stability)
[ ] Shelf grid: no axe violations (@a11y)
[ ] Shelf grid: filter chips have accessible names (@a11y)
[ ] Shelf grid: focus visible on tab through chips (@a11y)

## Tests to turn green

File: e2e/acceptance/shelf-grid.spec.ts
Run: npx playwright test --grep "@djk\.1" --grep-invert "@visual"
Run visual: npm run ui:qa -- --grep "@djk\.1.*@visual"

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
notes: Visual QA found only contract gaps — no app-side fix possible. Needs human review.

title: UI QA gate errors when zero Playwright specs exist
description:
## What's wrong
The ui:qa gate exits ERROR (exit 1) when no Playwright specs exist, even though zero specs is the legitimate expected state for an infra-only ticket.

## Where
Route: n/a. Project: n/a (gate runner). Element: gate script.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Have e2e/acceptance/ contain only .gitkeep (no specs).
2. Run npm run ui:qa.

## Expected vs actual
Expected: with no specs discovered, the gate reports a clean/PASS-equivalent status (0 passed, 0 failed) and exits 0, so infra-only tickets can pass the gate.
Actual: status=ERROR, topErrors=[No tests found], exit code 1.

## Evidence
Check: npm run ui:qa. Measured: passed=0 failed=0 flaky=0 new-baselines=0, status=ERROR.

## Severity
major: blocks infra-only tickets (e.g. shelf-proving-ground-513.4) from passing the visual QA gate despite having no UI to test.
close_reason: Fixed: run.mjs now detects zero spec files and exits PASS instead of erroring

title: Fixture system — in-memory API with URL-driven test states
description:
## Parent

shelf-proving-ground-513 (Fixture system)

## What to build

The complete in-memory data layer for the app, exposed as plain async functions, with a fixture system that switches data and behavior via the `?fixture=` URL parameter.

After this ticket, a component author can call `getBooks()`, `addBook(title, author?)`, `updateStatus(id, status)`, and `deleteBook(id)` against an in-memory store. A Playwright test can navigate to `?fixture=empty|error|slow|long|many` and the API responds with the corresponding deterministic profile. A Vitest test can call `initApi("fixture-name")` to reset to any state between tests.

Two files, flat in `src/`: `api.ts` (types, store, functions) and `fixtures.ts` (seed arrays per profile). Types co-located in `api.ts`: `Book` is `{ id, title, author?, status }`, `Status` is `"to-read" | "reading" | "finished"`.

Key behaviors:
- `addBook` prepends (newest-first), validates non-empty title (trim then check), default status `"to-read"`, author is optional
- `getBooks` returns the array as-is (newest-first by construction)
- `updateStatus` and `deleteBook` mutate in place; delete returns void, others return the full `Book`
- Errors are plain `Error` objects
- Fixture read once at module init from `URLSearchParams`; `initApi(name?)` resets the store for tests
- `error` fixture: every call throws (permanent)
- `slow` fixture: every call delays 2s via `setTimeout` promise
- `many` fixture: 200 books, `"Book 001"`–`"Book 200"`, UUIDs from index (`00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`), status cycling `i % 3`
- `long` fixture: 5–8 entries with stress strings (long single word, many short words, multi-author)
- `empty` fixture: zero books
- Default (no param): 5–8 seed books, hardcoded UUIDs, all three statuses represented
- IDs are UUID v4 — `crypto.randomUUID()` at runtime, hardcoded in fixtures

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `getBooks()` returns `Book[]` in newest-first insertion order
- [ ] `addBook(title, author?)` creates a book with status `"to-read"`, prepends it, returns the `Book`
- [ ] `addBook` throws `Error` for empty or whitespace-only title
- [ ] `updateStatus(id, status)` returns the updated `Book`
- [ ] `deleteBook(id)` removes the book and returns void
- [ ] `initApi()` resets to default seed; `initApi("name")` resets to named fixture
- [ ] Default fixture: 5–8 books, hardcoded UUIDs, all three statuses, deterministic
- [ ] `empty` fixture: `getBooks()` returns `[]`
- [ ] `error` fixture: every API call throws
- [ ] `slow` fixture: every API call resolves after ~2s delay
- [ ] `long` fixture: 5–8 books with truncation-stress titles/authors
- [ ] `many` fixture: 200 books with deterministic IDs and cycling statuses
- [ ] URL parameter `?fixture=X` selects the fixture at module init
- [ ] All behaviors covered by Vitest unit tests via `initApi`

## Blocked by

- shelf-proving-ground-513.4 (Project infra — Vite, React, TypeScript, Vitest)

title: Project infra — Vite, React, TypeScript, Vitest
description:
## Parent

shelf-proving-ground-513 (Fixture system)

## What to build

The minimal project infrastructure so that downstream tickets can build and test. After this ticket:

- `npm run dev` starts a Vite dev server serving an empty React app (a single root component rendering nothing meaningful).
- `npm run typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit` against app and test files.
- `npm run test` runs Vitest.
- `tsconfig.json`, `vite.config.ts`, and `vitest.config` are in place.

No app code, no components, no data layer — just the empty shell and working toolchain.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npm run dev` starts successfully and serves an HTML page with a React root
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` passes with zero errors
- [ ] `npm run test` runs Vitest (can pass with zero test files or a trivial smoke test)
- [ ] `npm run lint` works (ESLint configured for TypeScript + React)
- [ ] package.json scripts match the commands table in CLAUDE.md

## Blocked by

- None (can start immediately).

title: Shelf grid
description:
Fluid responsive card grid displaying all books with filter chips, newest-first order, staggered card entrance animation, and skeleton loading state. This is the spec — not buildable by itself; child tickets implement it.

## Filter chips

- **Interaction model**: "All" means no active filter. Selecting any status chip narrows the view; deselecting all chips returns to "All." Multi-select is supported (e.g. "To Read" + "Reading").
- **Visual**: Selected = accent fill (bgColor-accent) + on-accent text. Unselected = subtle border (borderColor-subtle) + default text. radius-full pills.
- **Order**: All | To Read | Reading | Finished (lifecycle order).
- **Spacing**: space-sm (8px) gap between chips.
- **Keyboard**: Each chip is a standalone button with aria-pressed. Tab moves between chips, Space/Enter toggles.
- **Position**: Scrolls with the page (not sticky).

## Grid layout

- **CSS**: grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(280px, 1fr)).
- **Max columns**: 4, enforced via max-width (~1280px) on the grid container, centered.
- **Gap**: space-lg (24px) between cards.
- **Page padding**: space-md (16px) on mobile, space-lg (24px) at 768px+.
- **Card height**: Grid default stretch (tallest card per row).
- **Filter bar to grid spacing**: space-lg (24px).
- **Responsive columns**: ~1 at 375px, ~2 at 768px, 3-4 at 1280px (natural from auto-fill/minmax).

## Staggered card animation

- **Property**: opacity 0 to 1 + translateY(8px) to 0.
- **Per-card stagger delay**: 50ms.
- **Duration**: --shelf-motion-duration-fast per card.
- **Easing**: --shelf-motion-easing-enter.
- **Trigger**: All visible cards re-stagger on initial load and on every filter change (re-key the list).
- **Cap**: Stagger applies to the first 20 cards only. Cards beyond index 20 appear at full opacity instantly.
- **Reduced motion** (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): Simultaneous fade (no stagger, no translate). All cards fade in together.

## Skeleton loading state

- **Count**: Always 6, regardless of viewport.
- **Appearance**: Instant (no stagger animation). Two text shimmer bars (title-height + author-height) + small pill placeholder (top-right, for status badge). Matches real card anatomy to prevent CLS.
- **Shimmer**: Opacity pulse between ~0.1 and ~0.3, using --shelf-motion-duration-slow and --shelf-motion-easing-enter.
- **Reduced motion**: Static at lower opacity (no pulse).
- **Transition to real cards**: Hard swap — skeletons unmount, real cards stagger in with the standard entrance animation.

## Empty filtered state

- When books exist but no books match the active filter: centered muted text "No books match this filter." No CTA, no illustration.
- The true empty-shelf state (zero books) is owned by the Empty state ticket.

## Accessibility

- aria-live="polite" region announces book count on filter change (e.g. "Showing 3 books", "Showing all 6 books", "No books match this filter").
- Filter bar: div role="group" aria-label="Filter by status".
- Each chip: button aria-pressed="true|false".

## Semantic structure

- main wraps everything.
- Filter bar: div[role=group] containing chip buttons.
- Grid: ul[role=list] with li per card.

## Ticket boundary

- **No page title** in this ticket.
- Grid renders **minimal placeholder cards** (title text, author text, badge shape, correct dimensions). The Book card ticket (shelf-proving-ground-i4m) owns the full card component (truncation, hover states, tap-to-open, dark mode details, etc.).

## Design decisions

- **280px card min-width**: Gives natural 1/2/3-4 column breakpoints without media queries.
- **20-card stagger cap**: Prevents 10s waterfall on the many fixture (200 books).
- **6 skeletons always**: Matches default seed count; simpler than viewport-adaptive count.
- **"All" as zero-selection**: Simpler state model than an explicit "All" toggle that combines with individual chips.
- **No sticky filter bar**: Avoids z-index complexity and CLS risk; acceptable UX cost for scrolling up to re-filter.

## UI acceptance

**Spec file**: `e2e/acceptance/shelf-grid.spec.ts`

**Fixture dependency**: No seed fixture produces a status with zero books, so the "No books match this filter" state cannot be tested with current fixtures. The first ticket must ensure the component renders this message when the filtered list is empty. The builder can add a targeted test in `e2e/agent/`.

Each ticket must list the acceptance tests it turns green.

### State inventory

| Element | States |
|---|---|
| Filter chip | all-selected (default), selected, unselected, hover, focus-visible, active |
| Grid | loading, populated, empty-filtered, animating-entrance |
| Skeleton card | pulsing, static (reduced motion) |
| Placeholder card | default, entering (stagger animation) |
| aria-live region | count announcement, no-match announcement |

### Acceptance tests (26)

**Behavior** (no tag)
1. Shelf grid: shows all books by default
2. Shelf grid: "All" chip is selected on load
3. Shelf grid: filtering by one status shows matching books
4. Shelf grid: filtering by multiple statuses
5. Shelf grid: deselecting all chips returns to "All"
6. Shelf grid: tapping "All" resets filter
7. Shelf grid: newest-first order
8. Shelf grid: keyboard can toggle filter chips
9. Shelf grid: shows skeleton cards while loading

**Visual** (`@visual`)
10. Shelf grid: chip visual states
11. Shelf grid: default populated screenshot
12. Shelf grid: skeleton loading screenshot

**Layout** (`@layout`)
13. Shelf grid: no horizontal overflow at any width
14. Shelf grid: 1 column on mobile
15. Shelf grid: 2 columns on tablet
16. Shelf grid: 3-4 columns on desktop, max 4

**Motion** (`@motion`)
17. Shelf grid: cards stagger in on load with correct tokens
18. Shelf grid: cards re-stagger on filter change
19. Shelf grid: stagger capped at 20 cards
20. Shelf grid: reduced motion shows no translate and no stagger
21. Shelf grid: skeleton shimmer respects motion preference

**Accessibility** (`@a11y`)
22. Shelf grid: no axe violations
23. Shelf grid: filter chips have accessible names
24. Shelf grid: focus visible on tab through chips

**Stability** (`@stability`)
25. Shelf grid: no layout shift when skeleton swaps to cards

**Performance** (`@perf`)
26. Shelf grid: entrance animation within frame budget

title: Fixture system
description:
## Problem Statement

The app has no data layer. Components have nothing to call for books — no way to fetch, add, update, or delete. Without this, no UI feature can be built: the shelf grid, cards, drawer, and FAB all depend on a working API. There is also no mechanism to put the app into deterministic test states (empty shelf, error, slow network, truncation stress, scroll stress), which blocks all Playwright and screenshot testing.

## Solution

An in-memory data layer exposed as plain async functions, with a fixture system that switches the data and behavior profile via the `?fixture=` URL parameter. The API is the single source of truth for book state during a session. Fixtures make every UI state inspectable, screenshottable, and testable without randomness or external dependencies.

## User Stories

1. As a component author, I want to call `getBooks()` and receive a `Book[]`, so that I can render the shelf grid without managing data fetching myself.
2. As a component author, I want to call `addBook(title, author?)` and receive the created `Book`, so that I can immediately update the grid without re-fetching.
3. As a component author, I want to call `updateStatus(id, status)` and receive the updated `Book`, so that I can reflect the status change in the UI instantly.
4. As a component author, I want to call `deleteBook(id)` and receive void, so that I can remove the card from the grid with confidence the book is gone.
5. As a component author, I want `addBook` to reject an empty (or whitespace-only) title with a thrown Error, so that I can trust the data layer enforces the minimum contract.
6. As a component author, I want `getBooks()` to return books newest-first, so that I can render insertion order without sorting in the UI.
7. As a Playwright test, I want to navigate to `?fixture=empty` and see zero books returned by `getBooks()`, so that I can test the empty-state UI.
8. As a Playwright test, I want to navigate to `?fixture=error` and have every API call throw, so that I can test the full-page error state and retry button.
9. As a Playwright test, I want to navigate to `?fixture=slow` and have every API call take 2 seconds, so that I can test skeleton loading and pending states on all operations.
10. As a Playwright test, I want to navigate to `?fixture=long` and get 5–8 books with absurdly long titles and authors, so that I can test truncation behavior and take stable screenshots.
11. As a Playwright test, I want to navigate to `?fixture=many` and get 200 deterministic books, so that I can test grid scroll performance and filter counts.
12. As a Playwright test, I want the default (no `?fixture=` param) to return 5–8 seed books across all three statuses with hardcoded UUIDs, so that screenshots are stable across runs.
13. As a Vitest unit test, I want to call `initApi("fixture-name")` to reset the store to any fixture, so that I can test each API function in isolation with known state.
14. As a Vitest unit test, I want to call `initApi()` between tests to get a clean default state, so that tests are isolated without module-reimport hacks.
15. As a developer, I want the fixture name read once at module init from the URL param, so that I don't need to pass configuration through React context or props.
16. As a developer, I want the `many` fixture to use deterministic IDs (UUID pattern derived from index), so that screenshots are stable without a random seed.
17. As a developer, I want the `many` fixture to cycle statuses (`i % 3`), so that filter-by-status tests can predict exact counts.
18. As a developer, I want the `long` fixture to include edge cases — one very long word (no wrap points), many short words, multi-author strings — so that truncation stress covers real failure modes.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Plain async functions, not hooks or classes.** The API surface is 4 functions (`getBooks`, `addBook`, `updateStatus`, `deleteBook`) plus `initApi` for test setup. Framework-agnostic — React hooks are a separate consumer layer.
- **Two files: `api.ts` and `fixtures.ts`, flat in `src/`.** `api.ts` owns the functions, types (`Book`, `Status`), and the in-memory store (a module-scoped `let books: Book[]`). `fixtures.ts` owns the static seed arrays for each fixture name. No folder, no barrel.
- **Types co-located in `api.ts`.** `Book` is `{ id: string; title: string; author?: string; status: Status }`. `Status` is `"to-read" | "reading" | "finished"` (kebab-case). No additional fields — ordering is array position.
- **Author is optional** (`string | undefined`). A book can exist without an author.
- **Default status is always `"to-read"`.** `addBook` does not accept a status parameter.
- **`addBook` validates:** trim title, throw `Error` if empty after trim. No other validation.
- **`addBook` prepends** to the array (newest-first). `getBooks` returns the array as-is.
- **Mutations return the full `Book`** except `deleteBook`, which returns `void`.
- **Errors are plain `Error` objects.** No custom error classes.
- **Fixture read once at boot.** The module reads `?fixture=` from `URLSearchParams` on first import and seeds the store. `initApi(fixtureName?)` resets the store — used by Vitest tests. In the browser, auto-init happens; in tests, `initApi` is the entry point.
- **`error` fixture fails every call** (permanent error state). No retry-succeeds behavior.
- **`slow` fixture delays all calls** (fetch and mutations) by 2 seconds via inline `setTimeout` promise.
- **`many` fixture: deterministic loop.** 200 books: `"Book 001"` through `"Book 200"`, UUIDs from index (e.g., `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`), statuses cycling `i % 3`.
- **`long` fixture: 5–8 handpicked entries** with specific stress strings (long single word, many short words, multi-author).
- **`default` fixture: 5–8 seed books** with hardcoded UUIDs, all three statuses represented. Exact titles deferred to implementer.
- **IDs are UUID v4** — `crypto.randomUUID()` at runtime, hardcoded in fixture seed data.

## Testing Decisions

- **Single test seam: the public API of `api.ts`.** Unit tests call the 4 functions directly after `initApi`. No mocking of internals, no testing of array manipulation or fixture selection logic in isolation — test the contract, not the implementation.
- **Good tests exercise external behavior only:** call a function, assert the return value or the state observed via `getBooks()`. Never assert on the internal `books` array, import order, or module-level variables.
- **Vitest unit tests cover:**
  - Each function's happy path (add, get, update, delete)
  - `addBook` validation (empty title, whitespace-only title)
  - Ordering (newest-first after multiple adds)
  - Each fixture profile via `initApi`: correct count, correct IDs, correct statuses, error-throws, slow-delays
  - `initApi` reset (mutate state, re-init, verify clean)
- **Playwright tests are NOT in scope for this ticket.** The downstream UI tickets (grid, empty state, error state) will write Playwright tests that navigate with `?fixture=` and test through the rendered UI. This ticket provides the data layer they depend on.
- **Prior art:** The `e2e/support/` directory has Playwright helpers (`fixtures.ts` for console-guard, `ui.ts` for screenshot/motion/a11y). No Vitest config or unit tests exist yet — this ticket will establish the pattern.

## Out of Scope

- React hooks or context providers — consumer layer, not data layer.
- Persistence (localStorage, IndexedDB, backend) — explicitly in-memory only.
- Edit title/author mutation (`updateBook`) — spec only has status change and delete in Detail mode.
- Undo/redo.
- Retry-succeeds error fixture (`error-recoverable`) — may be added later as a separate fixture.
- Sorting or filtering — UI-layer concern, not API-layer.
- Vitest configuration (vite.config, vitest.config) — infrastructure ticket.

## Further Notes

This ticket blocks three downstream features: Shelf grid (`shelf-proving-ground-djk`), Empty state (`shelf-proving-ground-y4n`), and Error state (`shelf-proving-ground-2s9`). It should be completed first. The `Sandcastle` label marks it as ready for an AFK agent build.
close_reason: All child tickets completed (infra + fixture system)
